topIssues.title: CI: repair develop scenario, script, and Windows framework failures
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Three required GitHub Actions jobs fail on develop commit d3d3bf29ea00e7efc9765a0d66d1a0496121408e:

- Zero-Key scenario runner: deterministic LifeOps scheduled-task scenarios route to REPLY, and the workflow scenario does not expose the expected Set-node run data.
- Scenario PR E2E: the build-agent-image contract test expects an obsolete immutable setup-crane action SHA.
- Windows CI framework-packages: provider qualification test fixtures use a POSIX-only absolute run directory, causing 27 assertions to fail early on Windows.

**To Reproduce**

Inspect Actions jobs 90970964715, 90970897272, and 90970660092, or run the corresponding scenario-runner deterministic E2E, packages/scripts test sweep, and scenario-runner test lane.

**Expected behavior**

All three jobs pass on Linux and Windows while preserving the existing fail-closed assertions and scenario outcome checks.

**Screenshots / recording of the wrong behavior (required for anything visible)**

- N/A - these are non-visual CI and test-harness failures.

**Evidence / reproduction proof**

- N/A - no visible UI behavior is involved.
- Backend logs: linked GitHub Actions job logs contain the exact failures.
- N/A - the reported jobs use the keyless deterministic proxy; no production prompt or model behavior is being changed.
- N/A - no persistent domain artifact is produced by these failing test contracts.

**Additional context**

Acceptance criteria:

- Update the action-pin contract to the workflow SHA actually reviewed and pinned.
- Make scenario-runner qualification fixtures platform-native without weakening path validation.
- Restore the three deterministic scenario outcomes.
- Run focused tests, the complete relevant scenario lanes, and repository verify.
- Open a PR against develop with the three failing job links and verification evidence.

topIssues.title: fix(ui): fade notification cards symmetrically during upward collapse
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Opening the Home notification shade fades newly revealed cards in smoothly, but reversing the gesture upward can make cards snap to a darker material and disappear without the matching fade-out. The card fill, content, and outline do not read as one continuous surface during the close gesture.

**To Reproduce**

1. Open the Home notification shade.
2. Expand a stacked notification group so multiple cards are visible.
3. Slowly drag upward to collapse the shade.
4. Observe the added cards during the first half of the close gesture and reverse/re-grab once.

**Expected behavior**

Cards that disappear from the rested shade fade out monotonically with the upward gesture, using the same physical card material throughout. Retained priority cards remain visible. Reversal, cancellation, and immediate re-grab restore/continue smoothly without a dark-material swap.

**Screenshots / recording of the wrong behavior (required for anything visible)**

Evidence upload in progress from the reproduced local preview; links will be added before review.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Complete disappearing cards fade with upward progress; retained rested cards do not.
- [ ] Fill, text, and rim stay on one material and do not snap darker.
- [ ] Direct reversal, cancellation, committed settle, and immediate re-grab remain smooth.
- [ ] Fanned rows follow the same fade model.
- [ ] Reduced-motion and existing gesture thresholds remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused component tests and real desktop/mobile browser gesture capture pass.
- [ ] Before/after screenshots, MP4 walkthrough, frontend console evidence, and manual visual review are attached.

**Evidence / reproduction proof**

- [ ] MP4 recording or JPG screenshots of the broken behavior — upload pending.
- [ ] Frontend console/network logs — upload pending; network is N/A because this is a local presentation-only gesture.
- [x] Real-LLM trajectory — N/A because no agent/action/prompt/model behavior changes.
- [x] Domain artifacts — N/A because no persistent domain state changes.

**Additional context**

The implementation should remove the gesture-only material transfer rather than changing gesture state, timing, or thresholds. The approved local patch is presentation-only and has no backend/API scope.

topPRs.title: release: promote develop to main (shared-tier shell probes + 249 commits)
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Production release: promotes `develop` → `main`, which deploys the Worker to `api.elizacloud.ai` and the Pages projects to the apex + `app.elizacloud.ai`.

## Why now

Headline fix: **Tier-0 shared agents 404'd every app-shell startup probe** (#17292). On a live shared agent the hosted app degraded through error paths — slash menu empty via a rejected catalog load, custom actions dropped, stream avatar warn, and the LifeOps capture loop re-reporting an "unexpected" failure on every signal. Production is the environment where that was observed, so the fix only helps once it lands here.

## Scope

- **249 commits**, 239 changed files under `packages/cloud/api` + `packages/cloud/shared`.
- **2 new production migrations**, both additive and idempotent — no destructive ops, no data rewrites:
  - `0183_lifecycle_execution_fence.sql` — `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` on `jobs`/`agent_sandboxes`, two partial `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, one `DO $$`-guarded CHECK constraint.
  - `0184_job_execution_leases.sql` — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS job_execution_leases` + FK + index.

## Verification of the headline fix on staging

Already deployed to staging (`api-staging.elizacloud.ai`, commit `2c3d63d3849`) and verified over **real HTTP against a real Tier-0 shared agent** created on staging (`6a2dc51c-767f-43a8-9684-d5ad2b19f3c4`, `execution_tier: shared`):

| Probe | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `GET runtime/mode` | 404 | 200 `{"mode":"cloud","deploymentRuntime":"cloud",…}` |
| `GET commands?surface=gui` | 404 | 200 `{"commands":[]}` |
| `GET custom-actions` | 404 | 200 `{"actions":[]}` |
| `GET agent/events?limit=300` | 404 | 200 `{"events":[]}` |
| `GET stream/settings` | 404 | 200 `{"ok":true,"settings":{}}` |
| `POST apps/overlay-presence` | 404 | 200 `{"ok":true,"appName":null}` |
| `POST views/chat/navigate` | 404 | 200 `{"ok":true,"viewId":"chat",…}` |
| `POST lifeops/activity-signals` | 404 | 503 typed capability gate (the status the client's stop-latch recognizes) |
| `POST conversations/:id/greeting` | 404 | 200 `{"text":"","agentName":"ProbeVerify","generated":false,…}` |

Negative controls on the same live deployment — nothing is masked by a catch-all:

```
GET  totally-unknown                    -> 404
POST totally-unknown                    -> 404
POST views/workbench/navigate           -> 404   (view this tier does not serve)
POST conversations/<other-id>/greeting  -> 404   (non-canonical conversation)
GET  runtime/mode  (no API key)         -> 401   (no synthesized 200 without auth)
```

Environment isolation also confirmed live: a staging-minted key returns 200 on `api-staging` and **401** on `api.elizacloud.ai`.

**Large.** This is a broad foundation PR (297 files) spanning calendar source
identity, availability, recurrence/timezone behavior, native Apple permission
semantics, Google watch lifecycle, immutable approval and mutation receipts,
household resource capacity, personal-assistant domains, one shared scheduler,
connector contracts, UI, benchmark provenance, and a SQL migration.

Primary risks are incorrect authority or tenant binding, duplicated external
effects during retry, recurrence/DST mistakes, stale source truth, webhook
abuse, accidental data disclosure across households/calendars, native
permission-mode drift, and UI states that hide a partial provider failure. The
new paths fail closed, use source/tenant/version/idempotency bindings, and have
focused real-PGlite and contract coverage; live providers remain a draft gate.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds the full world-traveling co-parent persona and G1-G48 test catalog, plus
  a 12,792-word implementation report grounded in 31 official, research,
  safety, and first-person sources.
- Adds source-aware calendar availability across selected Google, Apple,
  Microsoft, and ICS feeds, including health/freshness/provenance and explicit
  partial/error states.
- Adds durable Google push-channel bindings, strict notification validation,
  dedupe/order checks, scheduled retries and renewals, restart reconstruction,
  quota classification, and controlled 410 resync.
- Adds immutable calendar mutation proposals, exact owner/editor routing,
  approval CAS, replay receipts, series/version/tenant/source binding, Apple
  add-only semantics, and truthful invitation decline behavior.
- Adds deterministic caregiver/vehicle/restraint capacity solving with
  authorization, accessibility, freshness, handoff, transition,
  distinct-resource, invalidation, and shared-review constraints.
- Extends one shared `ScheduledTask` architecture and typed dispatch results; it
  does not add a second scheduler.
- Adds school-source reconciliation, household operations, family
  communications, food/inventory, parenting guidance,
  weather/routes/activity oracle, and childcare/work-scenario foundations with
  explicit source and safety contracts.
- Adds a calendar source manager UI and native permission presentation, plus
  desktop/mobile screenshots and a walkthrough harness.
- Fixes LifeOpsBench acting-agent provenance so adapter/provider/model are
  distinct from evaluator/judge identity and incomplete artifacts are rejected.

## What kind of change is this?

Features, improvements, tests, documentation, and one additive database
migration.

# Testing

1. Read the executive status and capability ledger in the report linked above.

## Detailed testing completed

topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Closes #17308.

## What changed

This integrates the reviewed latency/streaming work as one rebased branch on current `develop`:

- removes guessed chat, message-service, Discord, desktop proxy, and orchestrator generation deadlines;
- propagates caller/lifecycle cancellation through chat routes, message dispatch, model streaming, native bridges, local inference, Discord delivery, desktop IPC, Android and iOS;
- replaces orchestrator polling with ready/reconnected events and awaited shutdown drains;
- preserves upstream Discord exact-delivery receipts and audience attestation;
- parallelizes dependency-safe plugin/provider/database work, batches relationship entity reads, removes duplicate relationship ownership, and coalesces document authorization within the turn-owned memo;
- makes embedding metadata declarative rather than fabricating probe vectors;
- accelerates and owns Android Kokoro PCM/TTS streaming;
- keeps performance CI informational and removes threshold/ratchet/changed-source-test gating;
- adds real provider, chat-path, browser/PGLite, native, cancellation, and lifecycle telemetry/tests.

## Current exact telemetry

Latest 50-sample PGLite provider sweep on this branch (24/24 providers):

- fresh compose: p50 6.231 ms, p95 7.383 ms, max 8.017 ms
- maximum same-turn reuse: p50 0.058 ms, p95 0.096 ms, max 0.153 ms

- providers 10.392 ms; ingress 6.659 ms; delivery persistence 5 ms

## Verification

{"message":"Payment required to access this resource. Visit your billing tab.","type":"payment_required_error","param":"quota","code":"payment_required"}

The live tests deliberately fail and report that provider response. Nothing is mocked, skipped, retried behind a deadline, or reported as a pass. Re-run the existing live workflow after quota is restored.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): preserve active provisioning owners
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Closes #17215. Supersedes #17231 after deeper review of the sweeper/worker race. Refs #17162.

## Exact candidate
- head: `dbcf6798cf2c235eb42e7f5d05f899e3a87db068`
- base: `00d6f6cdaeb40d9d70e9664ebaccbd8169718f26`

## Summary
- derive owner, exclusive, cold-boot, and detached-execution classifications from canonical lifecycle metadata
- retain separate provisioning recovery and orphan cleanup thresholds while fencing recent terminal owners
- acquire the per-agent advisory lock and recheck CAS predicates before stuck/orphan/healthy reconciliation mutations
- add a durable renewable execution lease keyed by job, owner, and monotonically increasing generation
- install claim and lease atomically, renew while provider work is active, and fence destructive mutations and settlement on the exact live generation
- keep timed-out execution supervised so its eventual settlement remains observable instead of abandoning an unknown side effect
- add migration, repository, lifecycle, recovery, and PGlite coverage for takeover and stale-owner races

## Root cause
Job status is not an execution lease. Provider work may outlive a local timeout or worker process, so a terminal-looking row cannot prove that side effects have quiesced. The earlier bulk recovery also raced lifecycle enqueue because it did not participate in the per-agent advisory lock. This candidate combines locked predicate rechecks with a durable renewable owner/generation lease, and only permits takeover after lease expiry plus the recovery grace period.

Provider APIs still cannot be made transactionally atomic with the database when they do not expose generation or idempotency tokens. The lease therefore prevents concurrent database ownership and stale settlement; it does not claim to undo an external side effect completed by a process that died before persisting its result.

## Validation

- stuck-job PGlite suite: 10 passed
- repository/PII fixtures: 19 passed
- Cloud Shared typecheck: passed
- Biome and migration schema checks: passed
- fresh migration applied to PGlite: passed
- fresh exact-head CI is required before ready-for-review

A later local rerun was blocked by a concurrent, unrelated in-progress plugin-sql export edit in the shared checkout. The successful scoped results above were captured before that transient workspace mismatch; this PR remains draft pending clean exact-head CI and independent review.

topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Closes #17138. Supersedes #17232 after review found pagination, visibility, fallback-result, adapter-parity, and scale defects.

## Summary
- move document visibility/filter/query/count/pagination into one versioned adapter capability
- execute SQL listing as one snapshot-coherent CTE with database-precision-safe cursor ordering
- use stable millisecond-truncated `(createdAt, id)` SQL cursors that cannot skip microsecond rows
- filter canonical DOCUMENT memories and enforce bounded limit/offset plus supporting indexes
- implement the exact capability in both first-party in-memory adapters and fail closed before reads when it is unavailable or version-mismatched
- return structured `ok`, `query_miss`, `filter_miss`, `page_exhausted`, and `empty_store` outcomes
- keep matched `documents` distinct from coherently paginated `availableDocuments` fallback pages
- restore global `entityId` parity while retaining SQL requester/RLS context
- resolve requester role once and fail fast with `ElizaError` plus `reportError`

## Root cause
The original action-only fallback solved one message while preserving a bounded-page blind spot. The first deeper rewrite then scanned the entire corpus and performed per-document authorization lookups. This head makes filtered listing a database contract: one bounded query, exact totals, stable cursors, and explicit outcome semantics consumed by the action.

## Validation
